favourite.heading: Why Missouri can pull away
bullets: Missouri is the better football team by 4.0 points on opponent-adjusted results — but about 74% of that rating is still last season carried forward, and in a portal era last season is a different team (-4.0 pts).
Stylistically the matchup favours Missouri by 1.4 points: ball control vs front disruption (-1.4 pts).

underdog.heading: Why Mississippi State can keep it close
bullets: Playing at Mississippi State is worth 4.1 points — the league-wide home-field number, because a per-venue table was tested and could not be told apart from the home team’s own quality (+4.1 pts).
The outcome range is 15.3 points wide at one sigma — p10 -24.3 to p90 +19.7 for Mississippi State, so a projection of -1.3 still produces results a long way either side of it.
It is early enough that both ratings still lean on preseason belief — it widens the outcome range by about 4%.
College ratings are built on twelve-game seasons against wildly uneven schedules; even a clean rating gap carries more estimation error than the number implies.
